items.checks: Read all five mathematical modules and full materials. The explicit r(1-e)b formula is a genuine quotient lift: the full ideal eR is proved killed before constructing it. The right-inverse identity and the actual kernel-product LinearEquiv include both inverse equations and no added module finiteness.

Finite presentation of R/I is derived from I.FG and the actual quotient kernel. All prime splittings supply all maximal splittings for the pinned local splitting theorem. The split finite-free map then gives projectivity; splitting the actual R→R/I produces and verifies the actual idempotent generator 1-s(1bar). This is a complete allowed alternative proof, without conflating cyclicity and finite presentation.

Actual kernel equivalence and section differences produce both directions of the Hom(C,A) parameterization. The compatible-isomorphism subtype fixes the original inclusion and projection; both inverse classification identities and change of origin are proved. Nonemptiness uses the supplied actual section.

Read the complete reused Boolean-product proof. It constructs the finite-support ideal, actual exact row, rank-one free middle term and nonzero cyclic quotient. The local dichotomy is proved at an arbitrary prime, not merely evaluation primes, and both fraction-module and tensor localized maps are linked to q. Every global section and every compatible decomposition are excluded.
The same actual ideal satisfies I²=I because every element is Boolean, with nonzero quotient and the already proved exclusion of all sections. No finite-generation hypothesis leaks from S2.

Actual localizations at f_i and f_i f_j and actual induced maps are used. Denominator clearing, overlap torsion and a common finite exponent per original element give a unit-ideal weighted gluing with uniqueness. The unique values are proved additive and R-linear, and full localized maps, not just chosen representatives, coincide with the supplied sections. Compatibility is equivalent to equality of maps on the common localization. No finite presentation or uniform denominator over all source elements is assumed.
